definition: In this historical psychology usage, consonance is the relatively unified overall impression made by a compound tone or chord, as opposed to the more diverse impression called dissonance. It was commonly associated with pleasantness, and in musical harmony it referred to intervals counted as perfect or imperfect consonances.
